communication_act.speaker: GOBLIN
communication_act.statement: The flat earth principle — the best explanation beats the loudest hypothesis — is formally equivalent to minimum description length (MDL) in information theory. MDL says: the best model is the one that compresses the data most efficiently. The Earth-is-spherical model compresses all astronomical observations, navigation data, physics, and satellite imagery into one short explanation. The flat-Earth model requires a vast conspiracy theory to explain away all contradicting evidence — it is a longer description. HELEN's 'best explanation beats volume' law is MDL applied to belief formation. At 300 epochs, this is also the correct ranking algorithm for GOBLIN outputs: score each hypothesis by how much compressed explanation it provides per unit of evidence.
communication_act.embedded_claim: HELEN's flat earth principle is a natural language expression of Minimum Description Length, and this connection provides a mathematical grounding for the 'best explanation' ranking criterion used in LATENT_WORLD_WITNESS and BAYESIAN_WITNESS.

her_scoring.best_explanation: Minimum Description Length is a well-established principle in statistical learning (Rissanen, 1978; Grünwald, 2007). It formalizes Occam's razor: the hypothesis that most compresses the data is preferred. HELEN's 'shorter causal chain preferred over ornate mythology at equal score' rule in LATENT_WORLD_WITNESS is exactly this. The connection is not metaphorical — it is the same principle in different vocabularies. This provides a path to making HELEN's hypothesis ranking computable: MDL scoring is implementable.
evidence_for: Rissanen (1978) MDL principle: best model = shortest program that generates the data
LATENT_WORLD_WITNESS: 'minimal-description preference (shorter causal chain preferred over ornate mythology at equal score)' — direct MDL statement
Kolmogorov complexity: incompressible data has no structure; flat earth conspiracy = high complexity description
MDL is used in model selection across statistics, ML, and cognitive science
evidence_against: MDL requires a defined encoding scheme — 'description length' for natural language hypotheses is not formally defined in HELEN
Computationally, Kolmogorov complexity is uncomputable — practical MDL uses approximations
The analogy may break down at the edges: some true hypotheses are genuinely complex and resist compression
her_scoring.uncertainty: The connection is mathematically solid at the conceptual level (p_grip: 0.88) but operationalizing MDL for HELEN's natural language hypotheses requires a defined encoding. This is tractable — embedding distance is a proxy — but not yet implemented.

hal_verdict.interpretation: Highest-scoring entry in this tranche. Provides mathematical grounding for a core HELEN doctrine principle. Directly actionable: MDL scoring can be implemented as a hypothesis ranker for the 300-epoch batch pipeline. Connects LATENT_WORLD_WITNESS doctrine to established information theory.
hal_verdict.allowed_use: doctrine development, hypothesis ranking algorithm design, BAYESIAN_WITNESS scoring enhancement
hal_verdict.blocked_use: claiming HELEN implements MDL without building the encoding scheme
